props.title: Growth & Quality
props.sub: is the growth real — and does it become cash?

props.title: Three years of revenue
props.note: Revenue more than doubled in two years — a compound annual growth rate of about 57%.

props.big: CAGR is the one steady yearly rate that connects the start to the end.
props.sub: It smooths bumpy years into a single 'speed'. Ardee's revenue CAGR is about 57% a year.

props.big: Growth is only good if it earns more than it costs — and turns into cash.
props.sub: Chasing revenue with heavy debt and no cash profit is how fast-growing companies go bust.

props.title: The cash left after keeping the lights on
props.name: Free cash flow  =  Operating cash flow  −  Capital spending

result.label: Free cash flow — truly surplus cash

props.note: Illustrative. Fast-growing firms spend heavily on capacity, so FCF is often thin — that's fine, if intentional.

props.big: Does the paper profit actually show up as cash in the bank?
props.sub: Compare cash from operations to net profit. A healthy business converts most of its profit to cash.

props.big: Working capital is the cash trapped in day-to-day operations.
props.sub: Money stuck in unpaid invoices and unsold stock. The less trapped, the healthier the business.

props.big: Great quality = growing, high returns, converts profit to cash, low debt.
props.sub: Ardee scores well on growth and returns; the things to watch are its cash conversion and debt.

Quality = growing + high returns + cash + low debt
